# yopl — Full API Reference

`yopl` is an ES6 mini-library implementing a Prolog-style logic solver in JavaScript. It
provides rule-based logic programming with multiple driver styles and a built-in rule library.
Unification is delegated to [`deep6`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/deep6) — yopl's only
runtime dependency, itself a zero-dependency library.

## Concepts

- **Goal** — one of: a string (rule name with no args), a structured term `{name, args}`, or
  an inline JS function `(env, goals, stack) => boolean | null | GoalFrame`. Returning `null`
  succeeds without introducing new goals (useful for control predicates like `cut`). Under the
  async drivers (`solvers/async.js`, `solvers/asyncGen.js`) inline goals may also return a
  `Promise` that resolves to any of the above — the proof loop `await`s it.
- **Rule** — a function (or array of functions for a disjunction) that receives a fresh batch
  of logical variables and returns an array of terms. The first element is the rule head
  (`{args: [...]}`); the rest are body goals.
- **Rule database** — a `{name: rule}` object. Spread the built-in libraries to compose them.

## Solvers

### `yopl` — `src/solve.js`

```js
import solve from 'yopl';
solve(rules, name, args, env => { /* per solution */ });
```

Synchronous callback-style solver. Main public entry point.

### `yopl/solvers/gen.js`

```js
import gen from 'yopl/solvers/gen.js';
for (const env of gen(rules, name, args)) { /* … */ }
```

Synchronous generator. Supports lazy enumeration — break out of the loop to stop after the
first match.

### `yopl/solvers/async.js`

```js
import asyncSolve from 'yopl/solvers/async.js';
await asyncSolve(rules, name, args, async env => { /* … */ });
```

Async callback solver — for predicates that need to `await`.

### `yopl/solvers/asyncGen.js`

```js
import asyncGen from 'yopl/solvers/asyncGen.js';
for await (const env of asyncGen(rules, name, args)) { /* … */ }
```

Async generator solver.

## Rule compiler

`yopl/compile/` ships a pure-data IR plus two tagged-template front-ends: a per-clause DSL
(`yopl/compile/clause.js`) and a strict-Prolog whole-program parser (`yopl/compile/prolog`).
Rules are emitted as IR and lowered into the runtime shape `solve()` expects. The IR has
5 Term kinds (`var`, `wildcard`, `literal`, `cons`, `compound`) and 4 Goal kinds (`call`,
`cut`, `fail`, `js`). See `dev-docs/compiler-ir.md` for the design.

Public subpath exports:

- `yopl/compile` — IR + lowering + validation barrel. The recommended import for IR
  constructors and the lowering / validation passes.
- `yopl/compile/clause.js` — per-clause tagged-template DSL.
- `yopl/compile/prolog` — strict-Prolog tagged-template parsers.
- `yopl/compile/prolog/file.js` — filesystem-backed `prologFile(url, options?)` (sync) and `prologFileAsync(url, options?)` (async) loaders for `.pl` files.

The longer `yopl/compile/<file>.js` paths still resolve (via the wildcard subpath fallback)
but the three explicit subpaths above are the public surface.

### `yopl/compile` (IR + lowering + validation barrel)

Re-exported from `ir.js`, `lower.js`, and `validate.js`. IR constructors and helpers:

- `Var(name?)` — logic variable. Without a name argument, mints a fresh `Symbol`-named
  anonymous variable.
- `Wild()`, `Lit(value)`, `Cons(head, tail)`, `Compound(name, args?)`.
- `List(items, tail?)` — convenience that builds a cons-list from an array.
- `Call(name, args?)`, `Cut()`, `Fail()`, `Js(factory)` — goal IR.
- `Clause(head, body?, vars?)`, `Rule(name, arity, clauses)`.
- `collectVars(clause)` — declaration-order var name list.
- `IR_KINDS` — closed set used by the Lit-walker.
- `open` / `soft` / `_` (also exported as `any`) — re-exported from `deep6` for fine-grained
  per-value match control on `Lit`-wrapped values. `Lit(open({...}))` locks subset matching;
  `Lit(soft({...}))` extends both sides.

### `yopl/compile/clause.js`

Per-clause tagged-template DSL. `rule(name, arity)(...clauses)` returns an IR `Rule`; each
clause is built via `clause\`HEAD :- BODY\`` (body optional). The clause head is anonymous
(name supplied via `rule(name, ...)`). Inside a clause:

- Uppercase identifiers parse as logic Variables (`X`, `_user`).
- `_` is the wildcard.
- `[X | T]` is cons-list sugar; `[1, 2, 3]` is a fully-grounded list.
- `!` is cut, `fail` is the fail goal.
- `${...}` interpolates IR or auto-wraps:
  - in arg position: primitives → `Lit(value)`; IR nodes pass through; everything else throws.
  - in goal position: function → `Js(factory)`; IR pass-through; everything else throws.
- Strings can't span interpolation slots — wrap dynamic strings outside: `${'item' + i}`.

### `yopl/compile/prolog`

Strict-Prolog tagged-template parsers — multi-clause programs with the head functor in source.

- `prolog\`...source...\`` — parses a whole program; returns the lowered runtime `Rules` dict
  with the parsed IR attached under `Symbol.for('yopl.ir')` (importable as `IR` from
  `yopl/compile`).
- `prolog(source, options?)` — function form; `source` is a string (e.g. file content).
- `prolog(options)` / `prolog.with(options)` — configurator; returns a fresh tag closing
  over merged options. `{lower: false}` returns the IR dict instead of the runtime dict.
  `{operators: [{name, priority, type, target?}]}` adds operator declarations.
- `prologClause\`...\`` — single-clause variant; trailing `.` optional. Returns
  `{name, head, body, helpers?}` where `name` is the head functor.
- `prologFile(url, options?)` and `prologFileAsync(url, options?)` from
  `yopl/compile/prolog/file.js` — filesystem-backed convenience loaders that read a `.pl`
  file and forward to `prolog(source, options)`. `url` is anything `fs.readFileSync` /
  `fs/promises.readFile` accepts (string path, `URL`, etc.); UTF-8 is assumed. The async
  form is the right default for loading many files in parallel:
  `await Promise.all([prologFileAsync(a), prologFileAsync(b)])`. Lives in its own
  subpath so browser bundles without filesystem access don't pull in `node:fs` —
  Node, Bun, and Deno (Deno via its Node-compat layer) all run the module unmodified.

Body-context features beyond `clause\`...\``:

- Operators: `,` (conjunction at 1000), `;` (disjunction at 1100, mints `$or_<N>` helpers),
  `->` (if-then at 1050, mints `$ite_<N>` helpers), `\+` (negation at 900, desugars to `not`).
- Goal aliases: `=`→`eq`, `\=`→`notEq`, `==`→`eq`, `\==`→`notEq`, `<`→`lt`, `>`→`gt`,
  `=<`→`le`, `>=`→`ge`. Applied at goalize time so `X = Y` in body emits `Call('eq', ...)`
  while `foo(X = Y)` in arg position emits `Compound('=', ...)`.
- Op directives: `:- op(P, T, N).` (ISO) and `:- op(P, T, N, Pred).` (yopl `op/4` aliasing).
  Per-invocation scope; never leaks to the next call.
- Bare lowercase atoms in arg position parse as `Lit(name)` (matches yopl's runtime
  atom-as-string convention). The `clause\`...\`` form rejects bare atoms.

The two front-ends emit identical IR for the shared subset; the `prolog` form additionally
covers the body-operator and atom-syntax features above.

### Source-map support

`Clause` IR carries an optional `source: {file?, line, col}` field. Population is controlled
by the `sourceMap: boolean` configurator option on `prolog` / `prologClause`:

- **Default `false`** — no source attached to clauses; lowered fns and validator issues also
  lack source info. Saves ~50 bytes per clause (~2.8 KB for a 50-clause library, ~280 KB for
  5000 clauses) — production deployments that don't read source positions skip the cost.
- **`true`** — both front-ends populate `Clause.source` from the lexer's position tracker
  (1-based, counted from the start of the source). The `prolog` configurator's `file` option
  (silently ignored when `sourceMap` is off) populates `source.file`; `prologFile` /
  `prologFileAsync` default `file` to the URL when `sourceMap` is enabled.

The per-clause `clause\`...\`` front-end always carries source — each tag is one clause, so
the cost is negligible (dozens of bytes total across realistic usage). Programmatically-built
clauses (via `Clause(...)` directly) omit `source` unless the caller supplies one.

When `Clause.source` is present, the lowered runtime fn carries it as a non-enumerable
property so error reporters can attribute proof-time failures back to the originating clause.
Validator issues emitted against a clause with a `source` carry it on the `Issue` object and
append a `[file:line:col]` suffix to the issue's `message` for human-readable output.

Lexer position tracking is always on (transient memory, GC'd after parse) — gating it would
complicate the API for a marginal saving.

### `yopl/compile/lower.js`

`lowerRules(rules)` and `lowerRule(rule)` produce the runtime rule dict. Each clause is
walked per activation with fresh logic Variables. Re-exported from `yopl/compile`.

The **Lit-walker** descends into plain objects and arrays inside `Lit(value)` and
recursively lowers any nested IR node (`Var`, `Wild`, `Lit`, `Cons`, `Compound`). So
`Lit({age: Var('A')})` matches an incoming object's `age` field and binds `A` per
activation. `Maps`/`Sets`/`Date`s/class instances/`Wrap`-wrapped values pass through.
IR-node detection is gated on the closed `IR_KINDS` set, so user objects with a `kind`
field that isn't an IR discriminator are safe.

### `yopl/compile/validate.js`

`validate(rules, options?)` returns an array of issue objects. Issue kinds: `arity-mismatch`,
`call-arity-mismatch`, `undeclared-var`, `duplicate-rule`, `unresolved-rule` (opt-in via
`options.checkRuleReferences`). `validateOrThrow(...)` raises on the first non-empty result.
Re-exported from `yopl/compile`.

## Rule libraries

### `yopl/rules/system.js`

Generic logic-programming primitives.

**Term builders:**

- `head(...args)` → `{args}`. Build a rule head.
- `term(name, ...args)` → `{name, args}`. Build a structured goal term.
- `list(...args)` → cons-list. Wrap the last arg with `rest()` to splice an explicit tail.
- `listHead(...args)` → cons-list whose last argument is the tail directly. Requires ≥ 2 args.
- `rest(value)` → `Tail` marker.

**Inline goal builders:**

- `fail` — always fails.
- `halt` — aborts the proof search by clearing the driver stack.
- `cut(sys)` — Prolog-style cut. Pass the trailing `...sys` rest-args from the rule definition.
- `call(X)` — meta-call. `X` may be a string, a structured term, or a bound variable.
- `isBound(...vars)` — succeeds when every supplied variable is bound.

**`rules` object** — spreadable rule database:

- *Generic type tests:* `isVar`, `isNonVar`, `isNumber`, `isString`, `isNull`, `isUndefined`. (For JS-native type tests like `isArray`, `isMap`, `isSet`, `isDate` see `yopl/rules/native.js`.)
- *Equality:* `eq` (alias `unify`), `notEq` (alias `notUnifiable`).
- *Per-call options:* `unifyOpts(X, Y, Opts)` — runs deep6 unification with a per-call
  options bag (`{openObjects, openArrays, openMaps, openSets, circular, loose,
  ignoreFunctions, signedZero, symbols}`); env baseline restored before the goal returns.
  Pass options as `${Lit({openArrays: true})}` from clause source, or as a plain object
  at the runtime boundary.
- *Control:* `call`, `not`, `isUnifiable`, `conjunction`, `disjunction`, `true`, `once`.
- *Extended logic:* `counterExample`, `implies`.
- *Higher-order:* `map`, `filter`, `foldl`, `foldr`, `compose`, `converse`.

### `yopl/rules/native.js`

JS-native bridges — predicates over `Array`, `Map`, `Set`, `Date`. Compose by spreading
alongside `systemRules`. See `dev-docs/native-objects.md` for the full design and roadmap.

**Type tests:**

- `isArray(X)` — succeeds when X is bound to a JS Array.
- `isMap(X)` — succeeds when X is bound to a `Map` instance.
- `isSet(X)` — succeeds when X is bound to a `Set` instance.
- `isDate(X)` — succeeds when X is bound to a `Date` instance.
- All four require X to be bound; otherwise fail.

**Array:**

- `arrayList(A, L)` — bidirectional. Bind whichever side is unbound.
- `arrayGet(A, I, X)` — forward indexed lookup; A and I bound; out-of-bounds fails.
- `arraySet(A, I, X, A2)` — immutable single-index override; in-bounds replace or
  append-at-end (I === A.length); out-of-bounds with hole creation rejected.
- `arrayLength(A, N)` — A bound → N binds.

**Map:**

- `mapEntries(M, Es)` — bidirectional. M bound → Es is a cons-list of `[K, V]` pairs in
  M's iteration order. Es bound → M is a `Map` from those pairs (order-independent).
- `mapGet(M, K, V)` — forward lookup.
- `mapHas(M, K)` — membership.

**Set:**

- `setItems(S, Items)` — bidirectional. Both-bound case unifies as Sets.
- `setHas(S, X)` — membership.

**Date:**

- `dateTimestamp(D, Ms)` — bidirectional D ↔ epoch ms (TZ-agnostic).
- `dateComponents(D, C)` — bidirectional D ↔ component bag (local time). `C` is a JS
  object with optional fields `{year, month, day, hour, minute, second, ms}`. Month is
  0-based. Pairs cleanly with the Lit-walker for partial-bag pattern matching.
- `dateComponentsUTC(D, C)` — same as above, UTC.

### `yopl/rules/comp.js`

Comparisons. `lt`, `le`, `gt`, `ge` operate on bound, comparable values (number or string)
of the same type. `nz` succeeds when its argument is non-zero.

### `yopl/rules/math.js`

Arithmetic, all reversible: `add`, `sub`, `mul`, `div`, `neg`. Each rule defines a relation
between its arguments, and any one missing operand can be solved for.

### `yopl/rules/bits.js`

Bitwise: `bitAnd` (forward only), `bitOr` (forward + zero-identity reverse via `(0, Y, Y)` /
`(X, 0, X)` facts), `bitXor` (fully reversible plus all three XOR identities), `bitNot`
(fully reversible).

### `yopl/rules/logic.js`

Boolean logic: `logicalAnd`, `logicalOr`, `logicalXor`, `logicalNot`. Arguments are coerced
with `!!`.

## Examples

### List membership

```js
import {variable} from 'deep6/env.js';
import assemble from 'deep6/traverse/assemble.js';
import solve from 'yopl';

const rules = {
  member: [
    (V, X) => [{args: [{value: V, next: X}, V]}],
    (V, X) => [{args: [{next: X}, V]}, {name: 'member', args: [X, V]}]
  ]
};

const list = {value: 1, next: {value: 2, next: {value: 3, next: null}}};
const X = variable('X');
solve(rules, 'member', [list, X], env => console.log(assemble(X, env)));
// 1, 2, 3
```

### Append

```js
import gen from 'yopl/solvers/gen.js';
import {variable} from 'deep6/env.js';
import assemble from 'deep6/traverse/assemble.js';

const rules = {
  append: [
    Y => [{args: [null, Y, Y]}],
    (X, Y, Z, V) => [
      {args: [{value: V, next: X}, Y, {value: V, next: Z}]},
      {name: 'append', args: [X, Y, Z]}
    ]
  ]
};

const X = variable('X'), Y = variable('Y');
const target = {value: 1, next: {value: 2, next: {value: 3, next: null}}};

for (const env of gen(rules, 'append', [X, Y, target])) {
  console.log(assemble(X, env), '++', assemble(Y, env));
}
```

## Errors

The solver throws when it encounters an unknown predicate at proof time — a
typo'd rule name in either the initial goal or a body goal surfaces as a
runtime error rather than producing a silent zero-solution result. To stub
out a rule deliberately (without crashing callers that reference it), set
its entry to an explicit `null` in the rules object; the solver treats
`null` as "no clauses" and skips the goal silently.

## Conventions

- ES6 modules; `"type": "module"`.
- Single runtime dependency: `deep6`.
- 2-space indent, single quotes, semicolons (Prettier).
- Pure ESM source. CommonJS consumers can use Node's built-in dynamic `import()` —
  see `tests/test-cjs.cjs` for a smoke test.
